**Unofficial connector, not affiliated with Tilt Hydrometer (Baron Brew
Equipment).** It brings into Gladys the **Tilt** hydrometers floating in
your fermenters (beer, wine, cider, mead...), read from the **Tilt Pi** app
running on a Raspberry Pi on your network, through its local HTTP API,
without any cloud.

> **This integration has never been tested with a real Tilt Pi.** It follows
> the `tilt-pi` library used by the Tilt Pi integration of Home Assistant.
> Please report what you see on the Gladys forum.

## What you need

- One or more **Tilt** (or Tilt Pro, Tilt HD).
- A **Raspberry Pi running the Tilt Pi app** (the official Tilt Pi image),
  on the same network as Gladys, that shows your Tilts on its web page
  (`http://<Raspberry Pi address>:1880/`). The Tilt Pi listens to the Tilts
  over **Bluetooth**, on its Raspberry Pi: Gladys never uses Bluetooth (a
  Gladys integration runs in a container without Bluetooth).

## What you get

One Gladys device per Tilt **colour** ("Tilt Red", "Tilt Blue"...):

| Feature               | Unit                | Notes                                             |
| --------------------- | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| Specific gravity (SG) | none ("SG" in name) | the gravity, about 1.000 for water                |
| Temperature           | °C                  | a probe: kept out of the room temperature average |

- Gladys has no category nor unit for a density: the gravity is an
  "unknown" sensor without unit, its unit (SG) only written in its name. No
  unit is invented.
- The colour is the identity of a Tilt on a Tilt Pi: the device of a colour
  stays the same, even when you swap the Tilt of that colour.
- The feature names are in English; rename them at creation if you like.

## Installation

1. Install the integration from the Gladys catalog (Gladys 5.1 or later).
2. On the **Configuration** screen, enter the **Tilt Pi address** (the IP
   address of the Raspberry Pi, e.g. `192.168.1.30`, with `:port` only if it
   is not 1880).
3. Click **Test the Tilt Pi**: the message shows the gravity and the
   temperature of each Tilt.
4. Open the **Discovery** tab and add the devices.

## Configuration

- **Tilt Pi address**: an IP address or a host name, with a port if it is
  not 1880; `http://` is accepted, not `https://` (the Tilt Pi page has
  none), nor a path or a user. Give the Raspberry Pi a fixed address in
  your router. A new address is read at once (one request a minute at
  most).
- **Read interval**: 5 minutes by default, 1 to 60.
- No unit setting: the Tilt Pi API always gives the temperature in °F,
  even when its page shows °C (that is what the official flow of the app
  does). The integration converts it to °C, and Gladys shows it in the unit
  of your profile. If the API temperature disagrees with what the Tilt Pi
  page shows, it is not sent and the status says so.

## How often the Tilt Pi is read

- A read sends **one request**: `GET /macid/all` (every Tilt the Tilt Pi
  hears).
- **Never faster than the interval**, counted from the last read on a
  monotonic clock (a clock change never reads sooner): not by the test
  button, a reconnection to Gladys, an unchanged saved configuration, the
  Discovery tab nor a restart of the container (the instant of the last
  request is kept under `/data`, written before the request leaves). Before
  the interval has passed, the test button shows the last values and when
  the next read can happen.
- **Read only**: the integration never writes anything to the Tilt Pi.
- When the Tilt Pi answers **429 or a 5xx error**, it is left alone for the
  `Retry-After` it gives, else 5 minutes, then 10, 20...; always between 1
  minute and 6 hours, also across a restart.
- **No Tilt heard** (between two brews, or right after the Tilt Pi cleared
  its slots because a Tilt was silent more than 2 minutes) is normal: the
  Tilt Pi answers `{}`, the status stays connected and the known Tilts show
  "no recent reading".
- No answer, a page that is not a Tilt Pi (404, an answer that is neither a
  list nor `{}`) or a refused access: tried again at the next interval only.

## Which values reach Gladys

- Each reading is handed to Gladys **once**. A reading is told apart by its
  time (`timeStamp`, always given by the Tilt Pi), else by its temperature,
  gravity, MAC address and raw `timeStamp` (never by the signal nor the
  clock fields the Tilt Pi rewrites without a new reading).
- A reading at most 3 minutes old is sent as the current value; from 3 to
  15 minutes, it is sent **dated** (Gladys stores it at its time and no
  scene fires).
- A **silent** Tilt (out of range, flat battery, out of the fermenter) is
  **never shown alive**: when its reading no longer changes, nothing is
  sent, and the status shows "no recent reading". A reading dated more than
  15 minutes ago, measured with the Tilt Pi clock (the `Date` of its
  answer; the age alone decides, so a Raspberry Pi set back to an old time
  loses no reading), is never sent. Without a time, the first reading seen of a Tilt
  is not sent: only a reading that changed since the previous read proves
  the Tilt alive.
- A value out of range (gravity outside 0.950 to 1.200, temperature outside
  -10 to 60 °C, what a wort can reach) is never sent nor clamped; the status
  reports it. The 0 °F the Tilt Pi gives when its calibration fails is thus
  left out.
- **Two Tilts of the same colour**: without the "ID by MAC" option of the
  Tilt Pi, it has one entry per colour, filled in turn by both. The
  integration keeps a fingerprint of the MAC address of each colour: when
  it changes, nothing is sent for that colour and the status shows "MAC
  changed: two Tilts of this colour, or a Tilt replaced". A replaced Tilt
  (the old address never back) comes back when the same new address is read
  twice in a row. If an address already replaced comes back within 24
  hours (A, then B, then A again: two Tilts taking turns), the colour is
  **locked**: nothing is sent for it, and the status shows "two Tilts of
  this colour (MAC addresses taking turns): only one Tilt per colour is
  supported", until a single address has been read alone for 24 hours, in
  at least 12 reads (half the reads of a day at the chosen interval). The
  lock is kept under `/data`: neither a restart nor a saved configuration
  lifts it. **Only one Tilt per colour is supported.** The "ID by MAC"
  option of the Tilt Pi gives each Tilt its own entry (`RED:aa:bb:...`),
  read as the red colour; but if two entries have the same colour, neither
  is sent either ("two Tilts of this colour").
- A device created later gets the last reading, dated, if it is less than
  15 minutes old.

## What is kept under `/data`

The address read, the instant of the last request, the pause, and for each
colour met the key of the last reading seen (its time, or a short digest of
the entry) and an 8-character fingerprint of the MAC address of the Tilt
(never the address in clear), never the values. The file is
written at most once per minute, but for a pause or a new colour.

8 colours at most; 50 entries at most are read; an answer larger than 256
KB, or slower than 15 seconds, is dropped.

## External ids

`ext:tilt-pi:tilt:<colour>` (`black`, `blue`, `green`, `orange`, `pink`,
`purple`, `red`, `yellow`), then `:gravity` or `:temperature`. These ids
never change.

## Troubleshooting

- **"no answer"**: check the address, and that the Tilt Pi page
  `http://<address>:1880/` opens from your network.
- **"no Tilt Pi at this address (404)"**: another service answers at this
  address; check the port.
- **"no recent reading"**: the Tilt Pi has not heard this Tilt lately
  (Bluetooth range, battery, Tilt lying out of the liquid).
- Logs: the level is set with the `LOG_LEVEL` variable.

## Privacy

The integration only talks to the Tilt Pi, on your local network, over
HTTP. Of its answers it keeps only the colour, the gravity and the
temperature.

## Credits

Built after [michaelheyman/tilt-pi](https://github.com/michaelheyman/tilt-pi)
(MIT, Michael Heyman), the library of the Tilt Pi integration of Home
Assistant: the route, the fields and their units are ported to JavaScript.
Its notice is in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`. Tilt is a trademark of its
owner; this connector is free and unofficial.

## Parámetros de configuración

Estos son los parámetros que Tilt Pi te pide en su pantalla de configuración en Gladys.

| Parámetro | Tipo | Obligatorio | Descripción |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Tilt Pi in Gladys | `section` | No | Unofficial connector, not affiliated with Tilt Hydrometer (Baron Brew Equipment). It reads the Tilt hydrometers floating in your fermenters through the Tilt Pi app running on a Raspberry Pi on your network, by its local HTTP API, without any cloud: the specific gravity and the temperature of each Tilt, one Gladys device per Tilt colour. The Tilt Pi listens to the Tilts over Bluetooth on its Raspberry Pi; Gladys never uses Bluetooth. Read only: nothing is ever changed on the Tilt Pi. Never tested with a real Tilt Pi. |
| Tilt Pi address | `string` | No | The IP address (or host name) of the Raspberry Pi running Tilt Pi, with a port only if it is not 1880 (the port of the Tilt Pi page). Preferably give it a fixed address in your router; if it changes, enter the new one: the devices and their history are kept. |
| Read interval (minutes) | `number` | No | Each read sends one request to the Tilt Pi. Nothing reads sooner, not even the test button, a reconnection or a restart. |

## Cómo instalar Tilt Pi en Gladys

1. En Gladys, abre **Integraciones**: Tilt Pi aparece en el catálogo junto a las integraciones nativas, con una insignia de comunidad.
2. Haz clic en **Instalar**. Gladys descarga la imagen Docker (`ghcr.io/lm1lc3n7/gladys-tilt-pi:0.1.1`), la ejecuta en un entorno aislado del núcleo y genera la interfaz de la integración (dispositivos, descubrimiento y configuración).
3. Abre la pantalla de **Configuración** de la integración, rellena los parámetros y guarda.
4. También puedes instalarla directamente desde la URL de su repositorio: [https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-tilt-pi](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-tilt-pi).

Tilt Pi requiere Gladys `>=5.1.0`. El catálogo de Gladys se actualiza cada hora, así que una nueva versión está disponible como máximo una hora después de publicarse.

¿Todavía no usas Gladys? Es gratuito y de código abierto: [sigue la guía de instalación](/es/docs/) para empezar.

## Sobre las integraciones externas

Tilt Pi es una **integración externa**: una integración comunitaria empaquetada como contenedor Docker y publicada en GitHub. Gladys la instala con un clic y la ejecuta en un entorno aislado del núcleo. La publica y mantiene [LM1LC3N7](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7), no el equipo principal de Gladys.
